claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy will exhibit superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with conventional structural alloys.
The proposed AlCoCrFeNi HEA has a homogeneous, polycrystalline initial microstructure.
Casting followed by homogenization heat treatment can produce the proposed homogeneous AlCoCrFeNi HEA.
Replacing conventional structural alloys with an AlCoCrFeNi HEA will improve performance in hot, corrosive, mechanically stressed environments.
The proposed performance advantage applies under simultaneous mechanical wear and corrosive-media exposure at elevated temperatures, exemplified by temperatures above 600 °C.
The alloy's multi-principal-element microstructure promotes formation of a stable protective oxide scale.
The protective oxide scale mitigates localized corrosion.
The protective oxide scale mitigates wear-induced damage.
The multicomponent solid solution enhances passivation behavior.
Tribological stress causes a uniform and resilient oxide layer to form on the HEA.
The oxide layer self-heals under tribological stress.
Formation and self-healing of the oxide layer reduce material degradation.
The AlCoCrFeNi HEA will have significantly lower wear rates than traditional alloys under identical harsh conditions.
The AlCoCrFeNi HEA will have significantly lower corrosion rates than traditional alloys under identical harsh conditions.
Lower wear and corrosion rates will produce longer service life.
Phase instability or elemental segregation may limit the alloy's performance above its composition-dependent design temperature.
Multi-principal-element alloys have recognized theoretical advantages for degradation resistance.
